storyboard.ears: The fungus that caused the worst amphibian extinction in history never actually stopped spreading.
The fungus has affected 501 amphibian species, the largest disease-driven extinction event on record.
storyboard.eyes: substance: grey fungus on the frogs; cause: Data pours a bucket of sick water along the log and grey fungus spreads over every frog it touches
storyboard.evidence: Science | Amphibian species affected by chytrid fungus: extinct vs still around (count) | https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aav0379 | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: Thirty-nine percent of those affected species are still declining today, long after the fungus was identified.
storyboard.evidence: Science | Chytrid-affected amphibian species: still declining vs showing recovery (percent) | https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aav0379 | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: It has now hit 40 Australian frog species, proof the crisis keeps spreading to new ground.
storyboard.evidence: Science | Australian frog species hit by chytrid fungus vs untouched (count) | https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aav0379 | 2026-11-05

storyboard.ears: Extinction wasn't the end of this fungus. Species are still losing ground to it today.
